correctness.rationale: Reconstructed area and polar second moment from disjoint polygon, strips and vertex sectors. A strip has coordinates (c+u,v), 0≤u≤t, |v|≤s, and a sector has |x|²=1+2ρ cos θ+ρ² for |θ|≤α about the radial vertex direction and 0≤ρ≤t. Summing proves the stated A,J polynomials including the mixed terms. Rotation by 2π/n centers the body and makes covariance J I/(2A), so L⁴=J²/(4A⁴). Independently expanding with s²=1−c² and k=α/s gives the coefficients of j'a−2ja' in t as 0, (4/3)s²(ck−1), −2[k(1+2c²)−3c], −2(ck+k²−2), and no higher terms. The three nonzero coefficients are strictly negative because u=sin α−α cos α has derivative α sin α, f'=4 sin α·u, and g'=f, with all three zero at α=0. This gives strict decrease including comparisons with t=0, despite a zero derivative there. Expanding 2πJ−A² gives n²[cs(f/3)+4s(f/3)t+2g t²], with f,g>0; A∼πt² then gives L⁴−1/(16π²)=n²g/(4π⁴t²)+O_n(t⁻³). The polygon endpoint follows from J(0), and dilation by R replaces t by t/R without changing L. The proof covers each n≥3 and t≥0, not an n-uniform expansion. The two coefficient lists were independently expanded algebraically; the uploaded checker was inspected but not run. Its finite Green-integral checks do not establish the analytic sign for all parameters.

value.rationale: This compares a natural affine invariant along a canonical family of offsets of the basic planar polygons, distinct from the better studied perimeter and polar-area quotients. The all-radius strict ordering and explicit positive leading disk-limit gap are more informative than the disk moment bound or a numerical plot. The formula and sign certificate are reusable for this family; no broader monotonicity for arbitrary convex bodies is claimed.
